terms.definition: Expected return beyond an explicitly chosen benchmark or model; not a synonym for a profitable-looking chart.
Receiving a fill just before the market moves against that position, often because the counterparty has better information or timing.
The lowest currently displayed offer to sell on the specified book or consolidated feed.
The highest currently displayed offer to buy on the specified book or consolidated feed.
One hundredth of a percentage point; 100 basis points equals 1 percent.
A broker's required process for establishing a basis to expect shares can be borrowed where applicable; not an eternal guarantee of borrow availability.
A demand to return borrowed securities, which can force a short position to be closed.
Broker-calculated available capacity under account, margin and house rules; not the same as cash balance.
The capital or order size a strategy can absorb before its costs and market impact materially change results.
A statistical relationship in which a combination of nonstationary series can be stationary under a specified model and sample.
Locating trading infrastructure near exchange systems to reduce communication latency; access and cost are institutional constraints.
An issuer event that changes securities, ownership, distributions or symbol/quantity conventions.
Risk that an exchange, broker, clearing entity, issuer or other contractual counterparty fails to meet its obligations.
A venue arrangement sharing collateral across eligible positions; exact netting and liquidation rules are product-specific.
An order whose validity ends under the venue's definition of the trading day/session.
Excluding securities or tokens that later disappeared, potentially overstating historical results.
Long and short notionals balance; this does not necessarily make a portfolio beta-neutral or risk-free.
A deliberate exclusion interval in a validation design to limit information contamination; its placement and length need justification.
A simulation that processes timestamped data, decisions, orders, acknowledgments and fills in causal order.
An actual or explicitly simulated execution of all or part of an order.
Fill-or-kill order instruction: execute the required entire quantity immediately under supported rules or cancel.
Shares considered available for public trading under a data provider's definition; updates and corporate actions matter.
A contract-specific periodic payment mechanism used by many perpetual derivatives; distinct from trading commission.
Good-till-cancelled instruction, subject to venue expiration and corporate-action policies.
Orders or portions not fully displayed in the visible order book; absence from L2 is not proof of absence.
The quantity or notional relation chosen to offset a defined exposure; units and estimation method must be explicit.
The time range of observations needed to form a feature or realize a label; overlapping intervals can contaminate validation.
Immediate-or-cancel instruction: execute available quantity immediately under supported rules and cancel the remainder.
Collateral assigned to a particular position or product under venue-specific rules.
Delay between observation, receipt, decision, submission, arrival and execution; these are separate intervals.
Exposure created when a multi-leg trade executes incompletely or at different times.
Venue or broker forced reduction of exposure under collateral or margin rules; not the same as the trader's protective stop.
Using information in a historical decision that was unavailable at that decision's real time.
An order that supplies resting liquidity under a venue's classification; posting does not guarantee this status at execution.
A venue-defined valuation reference often used for derivative risk calculations; it differs from last trade and executable bid/ask.
The effect of an order's own trading on available prices and subsequent market behavior.
An operational classification of conditions such as trend, range, volatility or liquidity, estimated causally with uncertainty.
Value obtainable from transaction ordering or inclusion in blockchain systems; can change swap outcomes and hedge timing.
US national best bid and offer under the applicable consolidated quote rules; it is not an entire depth book or a universal crypto quote.
One-cancels-other linkage between orders; supported behavior and cancellation races depend on the venue or client implementation.
Outstanding derivative contracts or positions under a venue's counting convention, distinct from trading volume.
Selecting a model that explains sample-specific noise and fails to generalize.
Simulated order execution against a broker or local test environment; it does not establish real market fills.
Data representing what was actually known and available at the historical decision time.
An instruction intended to avoid immediately taking liquidity; it may reject or adjust depending on venue rules.
Removing training observations whose information/outcome intervals contaminate an evaluation period.
The order-ranking rule governing which resting orders execute first at a price; not universally simple FIFO.
PnL divided by a predeclared initial planned risk amount; state whether PnL and risk include costs.
An order restriction intended to reduce an existing derivative exposure without increasing it, under exact venue semantics.
Historical-looking indicator values or signals differing from what was observable in real time; causes and severity vary.
The difference between an observed value and a fitted model's prediction; it is not necessarily mean reverting.
Probability of crossing a specified capital-loss or insolvency threshold under a model; assumptions dominate the estimate.
An entry and subsequent exit of a defined exposure; partial fills and reversals require consistent grouping.
Producing and logging proposed actions alongside live markets without placing those orders.
Outstanding short positions measured under the reporting system's schedule; usually not a live tape of every short trade.
Difference between a specified expected/benchmark price and actual execution; the benchmark must be named.
Earning differences between purchase and sale quotes; inventory losses and adverse selection can outweigh it.
A statistical property of a process under a specified definition; a historical test does not guarantee future stability.
A triggered order that becomes a limit order; price control creates non-execution risk.
Evaluating only instruments or strategies that remain observable/successful and omitting historical failures.
An execution removing existing liquidity under venue rules, typically with a corresponding fee classification.
Minimum permitted price increment for a given instrument and price tier.
A maximum holding deadline even if no price-based exit has triggered.
Trading activity relative to capital under a specified definition; one-way and two-way definitions differ.
Repeated fitting on preceding data and evaluation on later data, with results aggregated from evaluation segments only.
An informal category of crypto assets associated with memes, cultural themes, attention, or communities; the label does not define transfer behavior, value, or legal treatment.
A chain/network and specific contract or mint, distinguished from a ticker, logo, wrapped representation, and native asset.
A protocol-defined relationship between traded quantities or state and price; parameters, real reserves, and virtual reserves must be distinguished.
A launch platform's transition criterion or event, often associated with migration to another trading venue; not a guarantee of success or safety.
Movement of trading state or liquidity to another pool or protocol, requiring identity and accounting reconciliation.
Pricing quantities used by some protocols that need not correspond to transferable assets actually held in a vault.
A defined estimate of supply available for economic trading after explicit exclusions; often uncertain and different from reported total supply.
A capability to create additional token units where supported; its presence and revocation are only part of the authority graph.
A capability to restrict token-account activity under the relevant program, distinct from general market illiquidity.
A mint-level privileged capability in the documented Solana extension, distinct from an ordinary holder-granted allowance.
Custom logic invoked during token transfer under a supporting token system; it may alter route requirements or reject transfers.
An informal label for token-level deductions or charges during movement; exact computation and recipients are contract-specific.
A change to the implementation used behind a stable contract address; previously reviewed behavior may no longer apply.
A representation of owners, roles, delegates, upgrade controls, timelocks, and dependent programs that can affect an asset.
A restriction on withdrawing specified liquidity rights under particular conditions; coverage, unlock time, and revocability must be verified.
A colloquial description of a token that attracts purchases while restricting or making sales uneconomic; a scanner result is conditional evidence.
An informal description of abrupt value extraction or abandonment harming holders; mechanisms differ and a heuristic flag is not a legal finding.
Activity from multiple identities or addresses that may be controlled by one actor; raw address counts do not establish independent participants.
Addresses grouped by an explicitly stated heuristic or verified label, with uncertainty and historical availability retained.
Following another participant's observable trades; follower prices, delays, costs, and inventory risks differ from the source trader's.
Behavior designed to make a wallet appear attractive to followers before unfavorable trades or inventory exits; discussed here as a defensive risk.
Activity flagged as possibly circular or non-economic by a stated method; not automatically proof of intentional manipulation.
One intended exchange of assets by an initiating trader, potentially implemented through multiple pool-level instructions.
An individual interaction within a route; several legs can belong to one economic swap.
The inventory that can be sold within stated cost and state assumptions, unlike market capitalization or a displayed last price.
The expected change in average execution economics caused by trade size under the quoted state, using a declared reference.
A bound embedded in an execution request, often expressed through minimum output; not a prediction or guaranteed realized cost.
An optional transaction scheduling payment under the applicable chain rules, distinct from swap fees and other tips.
An additional payment associated with certain submission paths or services; account for its actual conditions and currency.
A group of transactions submitted with service-specific sequencing and execution semantics; acknowledgement and final settlement are separate states.
The explicit rule governing when observations or transactions are treated as sufficiently settled and how reversals are handled.
The assets and eligibility information actually available at each historical decision time, including later failures.
Selection bias caused by studying only launches that reached a later platform milestone.
An operational comparison between measured attention and subsequent purchasing activity; generally an association, not identified causality.
Advertising or promoted placement that must be tagged separately from organic participation and security evidence.
Capital available at the current price under a pool's range or bin mechanics, distinct from all assets deposited in the pool.
A discrete price region or point used by some liquidity protocols, with protocol-specific allocation and fee behavior.
A measurement of how execution prices compare with later references from the liquidity provider's perspective, used to study adverse selection.
An explicit link between a contextual variant and its broader parent concept, preventing variants from being mistaken for independent discoveries.
